26635-the-rose-garden-husband.title: Rose-Garden Husband
26635-the-rose-garden-husband.creator: Unknown
26635-the-rose-garden-husband.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. So the Liberry Teacher braced herself severely, and put on her reading-glasses with a view to looking older and more firm. "Liberry Teacher," it might be well to explain, was not her official title. Her description on the pay-roll ran "Assistant for the Children's Department, Greenway Branch, City Public Library." Grown-up people, when she happened to run across them, called her Miss Braithwaite.

arxiv-2108-07408.title: Learning Dynamic Interpolation for Extremely Sparse Light Fields with Wide Baselines
arxiv-2108-07408.creator: Mantang Guo, Jing Jin, Hui Liu, Junhui Hou, Department of Computer Science, City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
arxiv-2108-07408.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mantang Guo, Jing Jin, Hui Liu, Junhui Hou, Department of Computer Science, City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR. In this paper, we tackle the problem of dense light field (LF) reconstruction from sparsely-sampled ones with wide baselines and propose a learnable model, namely dynamic interpolation, to replace the commonly-used geometry warping operation.

arxiv-2203-13579.title: Extracting the Λ \Lambda Polarizing Fragmentation Function from Belle e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} Data Within the TMD Formalism
arxiv-2203-13579.creator: Marco Zaccheddu 1,2,∗, Umberto D’Alesio 1,2, Leonard Gamberg 3 and Francesco Murgia 2
arxiv-2203-13579.description: Abstract Data from the Belle Collaboration for associated production (with a light unpolarized hadron) and single-inclusive production of transversely polarized Λ \Lambda -hyperons in e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} annihilation processes allowed to extract within a TMD approach, for the first time, the Λ \Lambda polarizing fragmentation function.

arxiv-2204-01508.title: Nöther Currents, Black Hole Entropy Universality and CFT Duality in Conformal Weyl Gravity
arxiv-2204-01508.creator: Daksh Aggarwal 1, Dominic Chang 2,3, Quentin Dancewicz Helmers 4, Nesibe Sivrioglu 4, L. R. Ram-Mohan 5, Leo Rodriguez 4,5, Shanshan Rodriguez 4 and Raid Suleiman 3,5
arxiv-2204-01508.description: Abstract In this paper we study black hole entropy universality within the Conformal Weyl gravity paradigm. We do this by first computing the entropy of specific vacuum and non-vacuum solutions, previously unexplored in Conformal Weyl gravity via both the Nöther current method and Wald’s entropy formula.

arxiv-2310-03144.title: Implementation of atmospheric proton spectrum in GEANT4 simulations for space applications
arxiv-2310-03144.creator: A. Ilker Topuz
arxiv-2310-03144.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by A. Ilker Topuz. A major part of cosmic rays consists of the primary protons, and this portion plays a crucial role in the space applications such as shielding of spacecrafts. In this study, the proton flux values measured at the top of the atmosphere through the BESS-TeV spectrometer in 2004 are introduced into the GEANT4 simulations by using a probability grid that generates the corresponding discrete kinetic energies with a certain discrete probability.

arxiv-2403-19944.title: Binarized Low-light Raw Video Enhancement
arxiv-2403-19944.creator: Gengchen Zhang, Yulun Zhang, Xin Yuan, Ying Fu
arxiv-2403-19944.description: Abstract Recently, deep neural networks have achieved excellent performance on low-light raw video enhancement. However, they often come with high computational complexity and large memory costs, which hinder their applications on resource-limited devices. In this paper, we explore the feasibility of applying the extremely compact binary neural network (BNN) to low-light raw video enhancement.

arxiv-2410-05123.title: Upgrading SPHERE with the second stage AO system SAXO+: frequency-based data-driven controller for adaptive optics
arxiv-2410-05123.creator: Isaac Dinis, François Wildi, Damien Ségransan, Vaibhav Gupta, Alireza Karimi, Michel Tallon, Isabelle Bosc, Maud Langlois, Magali Loupias, Clémentine Bechet, Eric Thiébaut, Charles Goulas, Florian Ferreira, Anthony Boccaletti, Fabrice Vidal, Caroline Kulcsar, Henri-François Raynaud, Nicolas Galland,
arxiv-2410-05123.description: Abstract This study introduces a novel frequency-based data-driven controller for adaptive optics, using power spectral density for optimization while ensuring stability criteria. It addresses disturbance rejection, command amplitude constraints and system transfer functions through convex optimization to obtain an optimal control in an infinite input response filter form.

arxiv-2412-10008.title: Automated Collection of Evaluation Dataset for Semantic Search in Low-Resource Domain Language
arxiv-2412-10008.creator: Anastasia Zhukova, Christian E. Matt, Bela Gipp
arxiv-2412-10008.description: Abstract Domain-specific languages that use a lot of specific terminology often fall into the category of low-resource languages. Collecting test datasets in a narrow domain is time-consuming and requires skilled human resources with domain knowledge and training for the annotation task.

arxiv-2506-00461.title: Bridging the Gap between Hardware Fuzzing and Industrial Verification Conference: Great Lakes Symposium on VLSI 2025; June 30-July 2, 2025; New Orleans, LA, USA Great Lakes Symposium on VLSI 2025 (GLSVLSI ’25), June 30-July 2, 2025, New Orleans, LA, USA DOI: 10.1145/3716368.3735190 ISBN: 979-8-4007-
arxiv-2506-00461.creator: Ruiyang Ma ∗ , Tianhao Wei ∗ , Jiaxi Zhang, Chun Yang, Jiangfang Yi, Guojie Luo †
arxiv-2506-00461.description: Abstract . As hardware design complexity increases, hardware fuzzing emerges as a promising tool for automating the verification process. However, a significant gap still exists before it can be applied in industry. This paper aims to summarize the current progress of hardware fuzzing from an industry-use perspective and propose solutions to bridge the gap between hardware fuzzing and industrial verification.

arxiv-2507-06761.title: Finetuning Vision-Language Models as OCR Systems for Low-Resource Languages: A Case Study of Manchu
arxiv-2507-06761.creator: Yan Hon Michael Chung, Donghyeok Choi
arxiv-2507-06761.description: Abstract Manchu, a critically endangered language essential for understanding early modern Eastern Eurasian history, lacks effective OCR systems that can handle real-world historical documents. This study develops high-performing OCR systems by fine-tuning three open-source vision-language models (LLaMA-3.2-11B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B) on 60,000 synthetic Manchu word images using parameter-efficient training. LLaMA-3.2-11B achieved exceptional performance with 98.3% word accuracy and 0.

arxiv-2509-26530.title: Explainable and Resilient ML-Based Physical-Layer Attack Detectors
arxiv-2509-26530.creator: Aleksandra Knapińska, Marija Furdek
arxiv-2509-26530.description: Abstract Detection of emerging attacks on network infrastructure is a critical aspect of security management. To meet the growing scale and complexity of modern threats, machine learning (ML) techniques offer valuable tools for automating the detection of malicious activities. However, as these techniques become more complex, their internal operations grow increasingly opaque.

arxiv-2511-01466.title: SecDiff: Diffusion-Aided Secure Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding Against Adversarial Attacks Thanks: C. Zhao is with the College of Computing and Data Science, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, and CNRS@CREATE, 1 Create Way, 08-01 Create Tower, Singapore 138602 (e-mail: zhao0441@e.ntu.edu
arxiv-2511-01466.creator: Changyuan Zhao, Jiacheng Wang, Ruichen Zhang, Dusit Niyato, Hongyang Du
arxiv-2511-01466.description: Abstract Deep joint source-channel coding (JSCC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for semantic communication, delivering significant performance gains over conventional separate coding schemes. However, existing JSCC frameworks remain vulnerable to physical-layer adversarial threats, such as pilot spoofing and subcarrier jamming, compromising semantic fidelity.

pmc-10529239.title: Piloting a Spanish-Language Web-Based Tool for Hereditary Cancer Genetic Testing
pmc-10529239.creator: Deborah Cragun, Gretter Manso, Stefania Alastre Arcusa, Brenda Zuniga, Julie Dutil, Marcia Cruz, Tuya Pal
pmc-10529239.description: The delivery of hereditary cancer pre-test education among Spanish-language patients is impeded by the dearth of Spanish-speaking genetic counselors. To address this gap, we evaluated a web-based genetic education tool delivered in Spanish to provide information typically discussed during an initial genetic counseling session.

pmc-10571964.title: Exploring the Domestication Syndrome Hypothesis in Dogs: Pigmentation Does Not Predict Cortisol Levels
pmc-10571964.creator: JoAnna M. Platzer, Lisa M. Gunter, Erica N. Feuerbacher
pmc-10571964.description: Simple SummaryDomestic dogs have a wide variety of colorations, and previous research has found that, in certain breeds, coat color can be linked to behavior. However, it is unknown if coloration is connected to dogs’ stress responses. To explore this question, we studied dogs living under stressful conditions: an animal shelter.

pmc-10614308.title: CHESS 3: an improved, comprehensive catalog of human genes and transcripts based on large-scale expression data, phylogenetic analysis, and protein structure
pmc-10614308.creator: Ales Varabyou, Markus J Sommer, Beril Erdogdu, Ida Shinder, Ilia Minkin, Kuan-Hao Chao, Sukhwan Park, Jakob Heinz, Christopher Pockrandt, Alaina Shumate, Natalia Rincon, Daniela Puiu, Martin Steinegger, Steven L Salzberg, Mihaela Pertea
pmc-10614308.description: CHESS 3 represents an improved human gene catalog based on nearly 10,000 RNA-seq experiments across 54 body sites. It significantly improves current genome annotation by integrating the latest reference data and algorithms, machine learning techniques for noise filtering, and new protein structure prediction methods.

pmc-11334494.title: Declining number of general practitioners can impair influenza vaccination uptake among Italian older adults: Results from a panel analysis
pmc-11334494.creator: Alexander Domnich, Francesco Lapi, Andrea Orsi, Ignazio Grattagliano, Alessandro Rossi, Claudio Cricelli, Giancarlo Icardi
pmc-11334494.description: BackgroundSeasonal influenza vaccination coverage in Italian older adults is insufficient and well below the minimum target of 75%. In Italy, most influenza vaccine doses are administered by general practitioners (GPs), whose number has been declining. In parallel, the number of patients per GP and GP workload increased dramatically, which theoretically may impair vaccination counselling.

pmc-11473142.title: Calcineurin inhibition rescues alloantigen-specific central memory T cell subsets that promote chronic GVHD. Reply.
pmc-11473142.creator: Ping Zhang, Simone A. Minnie, Geoffrey R. Hill
pmc-11473142.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). at 25 mg/kg/day for 14 days (1). Absorption was not validated by drug levels. Interpretation was heavily influenced by single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) analyses on day 14 with subsequent protein analyses, performed principally on CD8+ 2C TCR–Tg T cells. In contrast, our findings were primarily in alloreactive CD4+ T cells, with validation of expansion kinetics using small numbers of H-Y–specific CD4+ TCR–Tg T cells (2).

pmc-11475276.title: Inhibitory Effects of Fruit Powders on the Formation of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons in Charcoal-Grilled Pork
pmc-11475276.creator: Shang-Ming Huang, Bo-Chen Tung, Cheng-Hong Hsieh, Deng-Jye Yang, Ching-Wei Huang, Ling-Hsuan Chang, Kuo-Chiang Hsu, Ana Vulić
pmc-11475276.description: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), carcinogenic substances primarily formed through pyrolysis and oxidation of fat at high cooking temperatures, are commonly found at high levels in grilled meats. Reducing PAHs formation by incorporating natural antioxidants, such as through marination, has been demonstrated to be effective.

pmc-11502295.title: Current status and prospects of diagnosis and treatment for esophageal cancer with supraclavicular lymph node metastasis
pmc-11502295.creator: Qingxin Cai, Yingji Hong, Xuehan Huang, Tong Chen, Chuangzhen Chen
pmc-11502295.description: Patients with supraclavicular lymph node (SLN) metastasis from esophageal cancer encounter significant variations in treatment approaches due to differences in pathological subtypes and the lack of a unified regional staging system between East Asian and Western countries. The Tiger study aims to develop an internationally recognized staging system and to delineate the extent of regional lymph node dissection.

pmc-11651728.title: Staff education compared with active real-time waste segregation to reduce the environmental impact of hip and knee arthroplasty
pmc-11651728.creator: Rohan Prakash, Ahmed Nasser, Akshat Sharma, Deborah Eastwood, Mike Reed, Yuvraj Agrawal
pmc-11651728.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). AimsArthroplasty has been shown to generate the most waste among all orthopaedic subspecialties, and it is estimated that hip and knee arthroplasty generate in excess of three million kg of waste annually in the UK. Infectious waste generates up to ten times more CO2 compared with recycled waste, and previous studies have shown that over 90% of waste in the infectious stream is misallocated.

pmc-11678804.title: A Novel Objective Method for Steel Degradation Rate Evaluation
pmc-11678804.creator: Justyna Kasińska, Paweł Malinowski, Piotr Matusiewicz, Włodzimierz Makieła, Leopold Barwicki, Dana Bolibruchova
pmc-11678804.description: This article introduces a novel approach for assessing microstructure, particularly its degradation after extended operation. The authors focus on creep processes in power plant components, highlighting the importance of diagnostics in this field. This article emphasizes the value of combining traditional microstructure observation techniques with image analysis.

pmc-11689185.title: ABDOMINAL MYOSTEATOSIS IS ASSOCIATED WITH LOWER PROCESSING SPEED IN A MULTIETHNIC COHORT OF OLDER ADULTS
pmc-11689185.creator: Brendan McNeish, Iva Mijkovic, Matthew Allison, Timothy Hughes, Ilya Nasrallah, Eric Terkpertey, Caterina Rosano
pmc-11689185.description: Prior research linking myosteatosis to cognition in older adults has been conducted in relatively homogenous populations with narrow age ranges. We evaluated if abdominal myosteatosis was associated with processing speed and general cognition in a multiethnic cohort of middle aged and older adults.

pmc-12560577.title: Rhipicephalus sanguineus sensu lato infestation in an urban area in South Sacramento, California, USA
pmc-12560577.creator: Mario Novelo, Whitney Clack, Megan Siefker, James Brodigan, Francesca Rubino, Janet Foley, Sarah S Wheeler
pmc-12560577.description: BackgroundThe brown dog tick, Rhipicephalus sanguineus sensu lato (Rh. sanguineus s.l.), is an important vector of Rickettsia rickettsii, the causative agent of Rocky Mountain spotted fever (RMSF), in western North America, with the most prominent tick infestations occurring in the Southwestern USA and Northern Mexico.

pmc-13052563.title: Implementation of male-specific motivational interviewing in Malawi: an assessment of intervention fidelity and barriers to scale-up
pmc-13052563.creator: Katherine Ničev Holland, Julie Hubbard, Misheck Mphande, Isabella Robson, Khumbo Phiri, Dorina Onoya, Elijah Chikuse, Kathryn Dovel, Augustine T Choko
pmc-13052563.description: IntroductionTreatment interruption (TI), defined as >28 days late for antiretroviral therapy appointment, is one of the greatest challenges in controlling southern African HIV epidemics. Negative client–provider interactions remain a major reason for TI and a barrier to return to care, especially for men.

pmc-13218332.title: A forward genetic screen identifies Sirtuin1 as a driver of neuroendocrine prostate cancer
pmc-13218332.creator: Francisca Nunes de Almeida, Alessandro Vasciaveo, Arianna Giacobbe, Matteo Di Bernardo, Min Zou, Ainsley Mike Antao, Simone de Brot, Antonio Rodriguez-Calero, Alexander Chui, Alexander L.E. Wang, Nicolas Floc’h, Jaime Y. Kim, Soonbum Park, Stephanie N. Afari, Timur Mukhammadov, Nicholas Ortega, Sai
pmc-13218332.description: Using an unbiased forward mutagenesis screen in an autochthonous mouse model, we have identified new mechanistic determinants of aggressive prostate cancer. SIRT1 emerged as a key regulator of neuroendocrine prostate cancer differentiation and a potential target for therapeutic intervention. Introduction Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in men, affecting one in six men in their lifetime.

pmc-13301489.title: Combination Therapy with Bisoprolol and Tissue Protective Molecule ARA 284 Is Cardio-Protective and Improves Survival in Experimental Cancer Cachexia
pmc-13301489.creator: Masatsugu Okamura, Sandra Palus, Wolfram Döehner, Stephan von Haehling, Stefan D. Anker, Michael Brines, Jochen Springer
pmc-13301489.description: Background: Cancer cachexia is a serious condition during the last stages of the disease, which is characterized by the loss of muscle and fat mass in patients with cancer. There are no effective treatments for cancer cachexia, and new treatment interventions are urgently needed. We have previously demonstrated that 5 mg/kg/day bisoprolol and 1.

pmc-13556843.title: 643. A mechanism-informed clinical trial of psilocybin-assisted therapy for opioid use disorder: rationale and neurobiological framework
pmc-13556843.creator: O Mallon
pmc-13556843.description: BackgroundOpioid Use Disorder (OUD) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, with relapse remaining common despite the availability of opioid agonist and antagonist pharmacotherapies. Scotland continues to experience a disproportionate burden of drug-related deaths relative to other parts of the United Kingdom and Europe, reflecting the ongoing clinical and public health challenges associated with opioid dependence.
